newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade to consider all options in debt talks.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade to consider all options in debt talks.

text.p: Yugoslavia is prepared to consider all possibilities in negotiations with its foreign bank creditors to reschedule some $2 billion of commercial debt, a member of the negotiating team said on Tuesday.

Dragana Gnjatovic told Tanjug news agency that Belgrade would consider all options -- reprogramming or refinancing the debt, writing it off, converting it into commercial paper, buying it for shares or exchanging it for bonds.
Last month Belgrade said it would resume talks with the London Club of commercial bank creditors in Belgrade in the first half of September, but there has been no word since.
The two sides are trying to settle rump Yugoslavia's $2 billion share of the commercial debt left over by the former Yugoslav federation.
The talks are complicated by sanctions imposed on Belgrade for its role in the Bosnia war and arguments among the former Yugoslav republics over how to divide up assets totalling up to $100 billion.
Gnjatovic said the debt would have to be restructured so that the repayment burden would allow the country to service its foreign debt and at the same time secure foreign currency for imports.

According to the latest internationally accepted standards creditor countries should not allocate more than 18-20 percent of export earnings for repaying foreign debt if they are to keep developing while meeting their financial obligations, she added.
Any higher repayment burden would bring Belgrade into the debt trap in which the former Yugoslavia was stuck from 1983-89, she said.
Asked about the structure of the Yugoslav foreign debt, Gnjatovic said the largest part was to creditor governments grouped in the Paris Club.
